title: Non-equilibrium Muon Dynamics Imitating Fractional Spin Excitations in a Quantum Spin Chain
authors: A. Hromov, A. Zorko, M. Gomilšek, P. J. Baker, A. Prokofiev, M. Pregelj
abstract: Fractional spin excitations in low-dimensional and frustrated magnets are commonly associated with sporadic spin fluctuations, as observed in quantum spin liquids, spin ices, and other complex magnetic states. In this study, we investigate the spin dynamics in the amplitude-modulated magnetic ground state of AgCuVO$_4$, a spin-1/2 chain compound with competing intrachain interactions, by muon spectroscopy. Our data reveal a Gaussian decay of muon polarization that remains remarkably resilient against applied magnetic fields---a behavior often interpreted as evidence of emergent sporadic spin dynamics. However, density functional theory calculations of muon stopping sites and their quadrupolar level-crossing resonance spectra suggest an alternative mechanism: a two-state model where the muon randomly hops between two nearby sites, eventually equilibrating across both on a microsecond timescale via quantum delocalization. These findings provide a microscopic explanation for the field-resilient muon polarization and indicate that such behavior may not always stem from intrinsic spin fluctuations, but can also arise from non-equilibrium muon dynamics.
summary: This research investigates the spin dynamics in the magnetic material AgCuVO4 using muon spin spectroscopy. While initial data suggested exotic fractional spin excitations, the authors propose that the observed muon relaxation is better explained by the muon undergoing quantum delocalization and hopping between two nearby lattice sites. This work highlights the importance of detailed microscopic modeling to correctly interpret complex magnetic signatures.
main_problem: To determine the physical origin of the muon spin relaxation observed in the frustrated magnetic material AgCuVO4, distinguishing between intrinsic spin fluctuations and alternative dynamic mechanisms.
main_result: The observed muon polarization decay is best explained by the muon randomly hopping between two nearby lattice sites, a mechanism that mimics the signature of sporadic spin dynamics but is rooted in non-equilibrium muon dynamics.
method: The study combines muon spin spectroscopy (muSR) experiments with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to model local magnetic fields and quantum mechanical transitions.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 chain compound AgCuVO4, which exhibits complex magnetic ordering. The analysis utilizes a two-state model describing muon hopping between two sites, alongside theoretical frameworks like the Kubo-Toyabe and Gaussian-Broadened-Gaussian models.
key_observables: Muon polarization decay curves, Gaussian decay resilience to magnetic fields, and Quadrupolar Level-Crossing Resonance (QLCR) spectra.
important_parameters: Magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N \approx 2.0$ K), muon hopping rate, and local magnetic field parameters derived from DFT.
main_assumptions: The initial assumption linking Gaussian decay to intrinsic spin fluctuations is challenged by the successful fitting using the muon hopping model; DFT calculations assume specific exchange interactions (Hubbard repulsion U).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate temperature dependence of relaxation, polarization decay curves under applied fields, and the fit of the relaxation rate $\lambda(B)$ using the QLCR mechanism.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from initial $\mu$SR observations suggesting sporadic spin dynamics, through detailed analysis using LF $\mu$SR and QLCR, to finally proposing and validating the two-site muon hopping model using DFT calculations.
why_interesting: The work provides a crucial example of how experimental signatures (like field-resilient decay) can be misinterpreted; the rigorous application of site-specific calculations (DFT/QLCR) to explain the dynamics is highly relevant to understanding complex open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Temperature dependence of muon spin relaxation. (a) Crystal structure of AgCuVO4. (b) Muon polarization decay curves measured at various temperatures in zero applied field, along with the corresponding fits (see the main text for model details). (c) Temperature dependence of the low-temperature mean local magnetic field and of the fraction of the nuclear Kubo-Toyabe contribution. The solid line represents a fit to the Curie–Bloch expression [1 −(T/TN)α]β, while the dotted line marks the N´eel transition temperature TN.

FIG. 2. Muon spin relaxation in longitudinal magnetic fields. Muon polarization curves measured at (a) 2.4 K and (b) 0.09 K. In panel (a), the solid lines represent fits using the KT model for a longitudinal field, combined with exponential relaxation. In panel (b), solid and dashed lines correspond to fits using the two-state and GBG models, respectively. (c) Relaxation rates, λ(B), extracted from the fits as a function of applied magnetic field at different temperatures. Solid lines are empirical fits to bigaussian peak shapes (see Methods), while vertical lines mark the positions of their corresponding mean values. Thick dotted line denotes the calculated QLCR effect on muon polarization...

FIG. 3. Crystal and magnetic structure of AgCuVO4 viewed along two different directions. Panels (a) and (b) display the crystal structure, where atoms are represented as spheres: Cu (brown), V (green), Ag (light gray), and O (red). The muon stopping site is indicated by a dark gray sphere. Regions where the mean nuclear magnetic field equals 0.35 mT are highlighted in light yellow, while areas corresponding to a magnetic field of 2.8 mT (matching the experimentally deter- mined value at base temperature), associated with the mag- netic structure model with magnetic moments aligned along b, are shown in dark blue. Panels (c) and (d) display the cor- responding magnetic order.
